name: Dore Lake Fish'n Camp RV Park
note: Small private RV park on a narrow spit in the Hamlet of Dore Lake, beside the hamlet boat launch and fish-cleaning station, at the end of about 65 km of gravel road; it also rents cabins and parked RV units. The online form is a booking request, confirmed with a 50% deposit. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: Operator site dorelakervpark.ca (read 2026-11-19): rates.php 'RV - 30 Amp Full Hook Up Sites ... $50 per night, Weekly (7 nights) - $40 per night, Site rates include 4 adults'; facilities 'Pull Threw and Back Ins, Slide out friendly'; booking/index.php request form listing 16 'Full Service RV' sites (1-5, 7-17) beside 2 cabins and 5 RV-rental units; phone 306-832-2042. Rate is current: Wayback captures of rates.php show $48 in 2023-06 and 2024-08 and $50 in 2026-07 (and live today). Tourism Saskatchewan listing 3359 live ('full hook-up RV sites', 'Open May 15 to Sep 30.'). Google 'Dore lake Fish'n camp RV park' 4.8 (14 reviews) at 54.628593,-107.393383 with the same phone and website. Not on RV Life. Price indicator (posted rate) + presence (working website with phone) both met; C$50 is under the C$69 gate (no gateway within 40 km, gateways.py). Long-stay tests: no seasonal/monthly wording on any operator page (only nightly and weekly rates), nights sold directly, standing 2-night minimum only, no lots or homes for sale -> passes as far as measurable.
waterfront_evidence: Esri World Imagery (sat.py 640 m and 1.8 km frames, and satz z17, viewed 2026-11-19): the park fills a spit ~60-90 m wide running NNE into Dore Lake's South Bay. The angled pull-through rows at the pin (54.6286,-107.3934) sit about 15-35 m from the water on both sides, but the east side has the park road plus a continuous band of trees on the bank between pads and lake, and the west side a treed shoreline strip. Further north along the spit, trailers line the road 20-40 m from shore among buildings, docks and a treed east bank; no site map or numbering ties any pad to the shore. Operator photos (rv-park-photos.php, viewed): rv-0016a shows a trailer site with the lake visible through trees; rv-011a (from the water) shows RVs on a grass bank above reeds with spruce among them; rv-0018a a gravel fire-pit patio by the reeds and a dock (not identifiable as an RV site). No nightly pad can be named within ~50 m over open ground, so defaulted down to lakeview (unsure -> downgrade). 2026-11-19 --Claude

fees.note: Weekly stays (7 nights) $40 per night; site rate includes 4 adults; firewood and boat plug-in extra.

booking.note: The online form is a booking request (check the availability calendar first); bookings are guaranteed by a 50% deposit by credit card or e-transfer, balance on arrival. Campsite cancellations refunded 30+ days out less a $10 fee. 'Minimum two night bookings' sits in the general notes of the rates page.

Campsite same policy less a $10 cancellation fee') + /rates.php notes ('Credit Card Deposit to secure all bookings / Minimum two night bookings'), read 2026-11-19
flags: Pin: Google's point 54.628593,-107.393383 sits on the angled pull-through RV rows (Esri) - used. Tourism Saskatchewan's map point 54.625189,-107.380731 is ~1 km SE (wrong, as lessons warn).

Nightly share unmeasured: the operator's availability calendar (calendar/controller.php, per-site, Apr 2026-Mar 2027) shows every RV site 'Available' every night of May-Sep 2026, so it records no bookings at all. Nothing on the operator site or Tourism SK mentions seasonal or monthly sites (only nightly + a 7-night weekly rate), but imagery and a photo show trailers with wooden decks along the spit, which can mean seasonals.

Minimum stay: 'Minimum two night bookings' is printed once under the rates page's general notes (beside the cabin/RV-rental rules); it may be meant for the cabins only. Written as a standing 2-night rule (allowed); reviewer may prefer to drop it if a single RV night is sold.
Site count disagrees across the operator's own pages (21 / 18 / 16 bookable RV sites) and Tourism SK (15); stored 16 from the booking form.

Fit: no site lengths published anywhere; 'Pull Threw and Back Ins, Slide out friendly', imagery shows fifth-wheels/long trailers on the angled pull-throughs, and 34-35 ft rental RVs are parked on sites -> a 23-ft rig clearly fits; no max_rig_ft written.
Access: directions page says the hamlet is reached by Highway 924, '65km gravel'.
Google 4.8 on only 14 reviews (under 25), so presence rests on the working website + phone; price on the posted rate.
Facilities group omitted: no source says showers, washrooms, water or a dump station for campers (only the rental units' bathrooms and a glamping tent's porta-potty).
Waterfront borderline: if a site map ever names the shore pads, some north-spit sites might earn lakefront; defaulted to lakeview.
